title: Benchmark completes 2026 IOSCO audit with Type 2 assurance
gist: Promotional announcement: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence passed its sixth consecutive PwC Type 2 (reasonable assurance) audit against the IOSCO Principles for Price Reporting Agencies for the 12 months to 30 September 2026, covering lithium, nickel, cobalt, graphite, anode, cathode, black mass and rare-earth price assessments, with management citing heightened price-risk focus on non-China trade flows in energy and defence.

insights.claim: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence completed an independent PwC reasonable-assurance (Type 2) engagement against the IOSCO Principles for Price Reporting Agencies for the 12 months ending 30 September 2026, its sixth consecutive year of IOSCO assurance.
insights.speaker: Daisy Jennings-Gray, Matthew Bird
insights.so_what: IOSCO-assured prices are more usable as reference prices for offtake contracts and derivatives settlement in battery and critical-mineral markets.
insights.locator: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence Limited (“Benchmark”) is delighted

insights.claim: The audited Benchmark price scope spans lithium carbonate and hydroxide (including CIF North America and CIF Europe spot and contract grades), spodumene FOB Australia, flake and spherical graphite, synthetic graphite feedstocks (pet and needle coke), NCM/NCA/LFP/LCO cathode, graphite anode, cobalt, nickel sulphate and MHP, rare-earth oxides (NdPr, dysprosium, terbium, samarium, yttrium) and black mass payables.
insights.speaker: Daisy Jennings-Gray, Matthew Bird
insights.so_what: Ex-China lithium, black mass and rare-earth price grades now carry audited status, supporting their use as benchmarks for Western supply-chain contracts.

insights.claim: Benchmark added Type 2-assured rare-earth and cobalt grades partway through the period: Yttrium Oxide DDP China from 11 December 2025, Cobalt Metal Alloy Grade EXW Europe from 11 February 2026, and Yttrium Oxide CIF North America from 5 March 2026.
insights.speaker: Daisy Jennings-Gray, Matthew Bird
insights.so_what: New ex-China yttrium pricing coverage hints at growing Western demand for rare-earth price discovery amid supply-chain stress.
insights.locator: Reasonable assurance (Type 2) for the period 11 December 2025

themes.theme: Price risk in non-China supply chains

insights.claim: Benchmark's Head of Prices says ongoing volatility across strategic supply chains has heightened attention to price risk mitigation, particularly for emerging trade flows outside China in the energy and defence sectors.
insights.speaker: Daisy Jennings-Gray, Matthew Bird
insights.so_what: Demand for hedging and independent price reference is rising for ex-China critical-mineral flows; watch for new contracts and derivatives referencing these grades.
insights.quote: with a particular focus on emerging trade flows outside of China in energy and defence sectors
insights.locator: Daisy Jennings-Gray, Head of Prices at Benchmark said

insights.claim: Increased scrutiny of price benchmarks relied on by industry and government is raising the requirement for trusted data and transparent methodologies in critical-mineral markets, according to Benchmark.
insights.speaker: Daisy Jennings-Gray, Matthew Bird
insights.so_what: Government procurement, stockpiling and price-floor policies for critical minerals may lean on audited PRA benchmarks, entrenching incumbent price reporters.
insights.quote: With increased scrutiny over the price benchmarks that players across industry and government rely on
insights.locator: With increased scrutiny over the price benchmarks
